tasks.short: Organise images and past designs so colleagues can find and reuse suitable files.

steps.what: Collect finished files from the {DOCS} and the {OTHER} design editor.
Compare filenames, versions and duplicates in the {OTHER} digital asset library.
Enter campaign, subject and format tags in the {OTHER} digital asset library.

loop.input: Asset previews and existing campaign metadata; no identity matching.
loop.output: Suggested subject tags from an approved vocabulary.
loop.check: Reject unknown tags; retain source metadata; designer confirms suggested subject tags.
loop.stop: One proposal per asset, one retry on invalid output; leave unresolved tags for manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Campaign and format fields are deterministic; visual subjects in older files lack reliable metadata.

steps.what: Check licences, releases and reuse limits against records in the {DOCS}.
Set visibility and reuse status in the {OTHER} digital asset library.
Copy archive links into the campaign tracker in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} digital asset library for versions, access rules and reusable metadata, with a deterministic intake job from the {DOCS}. A bounded loop proposes missing subject tags; people confirm those tags and unclear reuse rights before assets become available. The {PROJECT} links to the library's campaign view, removing the copied index.
tasks.previous_blocker: Files had inconsistent names, incomplete rights records and no reliable connection between completed work and the archive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing library settings handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building intake adapters; a small classification loop helps with older unlabelled assets.
tasks.still_hard: Old licences, ambiguous ownership and meaningful version differences still need attention. GDPR applies to personal images; biometric identification needs separate assessment under Article 9.
tasks.human_edge: The designer recognises which version communicates well and which image is appropriate for a new context.

ambition.what: Self-service search of rights-cleared event images for event planners.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from filing to resolving rights exceptions and curating useful collections. The designer can recommend reuse, but gains no new authority to grant rights.

reach.task: Find suitable images for event invitations and signage.
reach.learn: Event formats, accessibility needs and the reuse restrictions planners must see.

evidence.claim: Archive intake, metadata inheritance, versioning and access rules are mainly deterministic work.
Bynder offers face-name suggestions with human confirmation; this design excludes face recognition.
GDPR Article 9 restricts biometric processing for uniquely identifying people.
In the Netherlands, certain employee-data and monitoring arrangements require works-council consent.

assumptions: The typical company has a digital asset library or a document store with comparable record features.
The time split follows the records-heavy prior; visual tagging and unclear rights retain human review.
Duplicate detection preserves versions and quarantines candidates rather than deleting files.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one library and one intake route.
National rules govern employee consultation where applicable; employee monitoring is outside the design.
unknowns: Available library interfaces and metadata controls.
Volume of old assets and completeness of licence records.
Whether a separate campaign index is maintained.
Who may approve reuse status and access changes.
Applicable country, consultation requirements and permitted model processing.
research_questions: Can existing library settings provide intake, versioning and metadata inheritance without custom code?
Which missing tags materially improve retrieval?
How accurately can approved tags be proposed on representative archive samples?
new_work: Confirm proposed subject tags and resolve unclear reuse rights.
Maintain tag vocabulary and access mappings.
Monitor failed imports and expiry notices.
Check that derivatives preserve rights metadata.

tasks.short: Prepare technical instructions and files for people producing final print layouts.

steps.what: Read the approved artwork and supplier specifications from the {DOCS} and {EMAIL}.
Inspect dimensions, fonts, colour and bleed in the {OTHER} print-preflight editor.
Discuss unusual finishes or conflicting requirements with the print supplier.
Write assembly instructions, page order and finishing notes in the {DOCS}.
Check production instructions against the artwork and resolved exceptions.
Approve and send the production packet through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Capture approved print requirements in the {WORKFLOW} and configure the {OTHER} print-preflight editor with supplier profiles. A deterministic generator combines requirements, preflight results and recorded exceptions into instructions in the {DOCS}. The designer reviews the packet and approves its release through the {EMAIL}, with the exact files and approval logged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier instructions arrived in different formats, and technical notes were repeatedly copied between artwork and documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Preflight profiles already support standard checks. Structured intake and inexpensive template generation can remove repeated transcription without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Special finishes, substrate behaviour and supplier-specific tolerances need production judgement. A technically valid file can still print poorly.
tasks.human_edge: The designer anticipates physical production problems and resolves trade-offs with the supplier.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into copying specifications and writing routine notes. More time goes into unusual print jobs; release authority remains unchanged.

reach.task: Assemble final layouts using a consistent production packet.
reach.learn: Imposition, colour profiles, font handling and the instructions production staff actually need.

evidence.claim: Enfocus PitStop Pro checks PDF/X profiles, applies action lists and reports issues.
Structured specifications can generate print instructions deterministically, with people reviewing exceptions and release.

assumptions: Artwork has already received content and brand approval.
Common supplier requirements can be captured as structured fields.
The document-heavy prior fits current work; routine note creation needs no model once intake is structured.
Automatic fixes are limited to approved, reversible actions on working copies.
Build ranges cover common print formats and a small set of supplier profiles.
GDPR applies to personal content; national consultation rules matter if implementation changes employee-data processing.
unknowns: Supplier profiles, accepted formats and unusual finishing requirements.
Available preflight automation interfaces.
Who can release production files.
How often incomplete specifications require supplier calls.
Access requirements and applicable national consultation rules.
research_questions: Which requirements can existing preflight profiles verify?
Which instruction fields prevent the most supplier clarification requests?
Does a generated packet remain correct across representative print jobs?
new_work: Maintain supplier profiles and instruction templates.
Resolve missing requirements and failed preflight checks.
Review generated packets and approve release.
Update rules after supplier feedback or print defects.

tasks.short: Develop visual sketches, discuss them with stakeholders and revise the chosen direction.

steps.what: Read the campaign brief and reference assets in the {DOCS}.
Draw rough visual routes on paper or in the {OTHER} illustration editor.

loop.input: Designer-written visual directions, approved references and brand constraints.
loop.output: Up to three rough visual routes for internal exploration.
loop.check: Designer checks relevance, visual defects, inappropriate content and reference permissions; retain provenance metadata.
loop.stop: Three routes and one revision round per route; return to manual sketching if unsuitable.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle known layouts but cannot illustrate a new visual idea from a brief.

steps.what: Select and refine promising sketches in the {OTHER} illustration editor.
Assemble and send concept proofs through the {DOCS} and {EMAIL}.
Discuss concept proofs and agree changes with the marketing manager.
Revise the chosen direction in the {OTHER} illustration editor.
Approve the revised artwork and record the decision through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to collect briefs, assemble proofs from the {DOCS} and record feedback against specific versions. A bounded image loop in the {OTHER} illustration editor drafts rough routes; the designer selects, edits and discusses them with stakeholders. Configure reusable components and export presets for revisions, while keeping proof sharing and artwork approval as explicit actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visual exploration required manual drawing, while scattered feedback caused repeated exports and uncertainty about approved versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Image generation can draft exploratory routes, and existing workflow settings can organise proof rounds. Faster integration work connects those pieces without automating the creative conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Originality, visual consistency and editable detail remain difficult. GDPR governs personal references; EU AI Act transparency obligations depend on the output and its use, and generated logo rights need legal review.
tasks.human_edge: The designer interprets vague reactions, develops a coherent visual idea and explains creative trade-offs.

ambition.what: Early visual-concept clinic for internal event planners.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less proof administration and more direction-setting with stakeholders. The designer can propose more routes within the same brief; final brand and publication authority do not change.

reach.task: Choose a campaign direction using audience goals and visual evidence.
reach.learn: Positioning, audience response and how concept choices affect campaign objectives.

reach.task: Develop an event identity before commissioning final collateral.
reach.learn: Venue constraints, signage needs and the timing of event decisions.

evidence.claim: Adobe Creative Studio generates and edits images and attaches Content Credentials describing their origin.
Figma Buzz supports locked templates and spreadsheet-driven variants.
A platform study found increased output among text-to-image adopters alongside reduced average novelty; this is not a forecast for this company.
EU AI Act Article 50 addresses machine-readable marking and disclosure for specified generated content.
The digest reports a German court denying copyright protection to three generated logos; rights cannot be assumed from prompting alone.

assumptions: This describes an in-house designer working mainly with a marketing manager; external-client proof release would require an external-action gate.
The human-heavy prior fits concept selection and discussion. The means split gives more time to the editor because drawing and revision are substantial.
Generated routes are exploratory drafts; distinctive logos and final craft may require manual creation.
Editor presets and reusable components support predictable revisions without a second model loop.
Build ranges cover one brief workflow and one approved generation route.
National consultation rules apply where employee-data processing changes.
unknowns: Whether stakeholders are internal or external.
Brand restrictions and permitted reference materials.
Approved model processing terms and retention settings.
Which generated uses require disclosure or additional rights review.
Who approves artwork and subsequent publication.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which concept types benefit from generation without losing distinctive visual direction?
Do exported proofs retain provenance metadata?
Which repeat revisions can existing editor components handle?
What contractual language is needed for generated elements in commissioned work?
new_work: Reject unsuitable generated routes and document selected references.
Check rights, provenance and applicable disclosure requirements.
Maintain brief fields, proof templates and revision presets.
Resolve feedback conflicts and verify approval applies to the exact artwork version.

tasks.short: Investigate design software and concepts, test promising options and share useful findings.

steps.what: Define the design problem and trial criteria in the {DOCS}.
Find documentation, examples and release notes using the {OTHER} web browser.
Read sources and compare capabilities, limitations and design examples in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Up to ten retrieved pages and the designer's trial criteria.
loop.output: A comparison with source links, supporting passages and explicit unknowns.
loop.check: Validate that links and quoted passages exist; designer opens every cited link and checks material claims.
loop.stop: Ten pages and two extraction attempts; report gaps and return unreadable or conflicting sources to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Capability descriptions and design arguments are free text with inconsistent terminology.

steps.what: Choose a concept or software feature for a practical trial.
Test representative artwork in the {OTHER} design editor or prototype environment.
Write and share a recommendation through the {DOCS} and {CHAT}.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects permitted sources and builds a cited research comparison in the {DOCS} through one bounded extraction loop. Deterministic test packs supply representative files and record repeatable checks, while the designer evaluates creative usefulness in the {OTHER} design editor. A report template combines verified findings and trial results for approved sharing through the {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources used inconsistent language, and comparisons were rebuilt from scattered notes without practical tests.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple collectors and report generators are cheaper to build. A bounded reading loop can extract comparable claims, while existing trial environments provide practical evidence.
tasks.still_hard: A polished demonstration may hide workflow limitations. Taste, accessibility, licensing, data handling and export compatibility need direct evaluation.
tasks.human_edge: The designer distinguishes a useful technique from a fashionable demonstration and tests whether it improves actual design work.

ambition.what: Monthly evidence-backed design-tool trial clinic for the marketing team.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated browsing toward focused trials and shared recommendations. The designer gains a stronger advisory role; purchasing and installation rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a design concept works in an accessible interactive prototype.
reach.learn: Keyboard use, responsive behaviour, interaction states and implementation constraints.

reach.task: Assess the value and cost of adopting a design capability.
reach.learn: Team training effort, licence costs and the evidence needed for an adoption decision.

evidence.claim: A cited answer desk with bounded reading and human source checks is feasible; the designer still evaluates usefulness.
Figma Make produces editable prototypes from prompts and a team's design system, providing one capability that can be tested.
Reported increases in image output do not establish novelty or suitability for a particular design workflow.

assumptions: Most source material is public and may be retrieved under its access terms.
The gather-heavy prior fits research; practical trials remain substantial and mainly human.
The means split favours browsing, documents and trial screens over meetings for individual research.
New software trials use approved environments and synthetic or cleared artwork.
Build ranges cover a limited source set and one reusable trial pack.
GDPR applies if trials use personal data; national rules determine any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Approved source access and trial environments.
Current software capabilities and export requirements.
Who authorises installation, purchases and data processing.
Which trial results the marketing team considers useful.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which sources provide verifiable technical claims rather than promotional summaries?
Which representative test files reveal compatibility and editing limitations?
Can current tools provide source collection and test reporting through configuration alone?
Does the comparison reliably distinguish documented capability from untested claims?
new_work: Open cited sources and correct unsupported comparisons.
Maintain source lists and refresh stale findings.
Update trial packs as formats and team needs change.
Record trial limitations and separate recommendations from purchase approvals.

role.altitude: The designer spends less time filing assets, copying print specifications and preparing proof rounds. More time goes into visual direction, production judgement and practical trials; final release, rights and purchasing decisions stay with their existing authorised roles.
reach: Help event planners find suitable reusable images and develop early visual concepts.
Give desktop publishers clear, versioned production instructions.
Work with web and digital interface designers to test accessible interactive concepts.
Give marketing managers tested evidence for creative and software choices.
skills_to_grow: Structured briefs, reusable metadata and template design.
Print profiles, production tolerances and exception diagnosis.
Asset rights, GDPR and generated-content provenance.
Critical source reading and repeatable software trials.
role.ambitious_version: Build a shared visual service that combines searchable reusable assets, reliable production packets, early concept clinics and tested design guidance. Broader access depends on clear reuse rights and useful examples; creative selection and stakeholder decisions remain human.
